app_prompt:
# Phoenix Elixir app benchmark

JobyKit is already installed. The app you build is the artifact being
benchmarked: a modern demo landing site for a fictional product of your
choice. It is not a tool for running benchmarks; no benchmark-themed
features or copy.

## Setup

1. In the current working directory run `mix joby_kit.new benchapp`, then work inside the `benchapp` directory it creates.
2. Remove the stock JobyKit demo content: the generator's `simple_nav` header and "built with" footer in `lib/benchapp_web/components/layouts.ex`, and the welcome content of HomeLive in `lib/benchapp_web/live/home_live.ex`. Keep the `/design` and `/custom-designs` pages.

## Requirements

Mobile and desktop views, and working light and dark themes, throughout.

3. A top navigation bar in `Layouts.app` with id `main-nav` that marks the current page's link with `aria-current="page"`, has a menu that works at phone widths behind a toggle button with id `nav-toggle`, and a theme toggle with id `theme-toggle` usable at both widths.
4. HomeLive as a landing page with a hero.
5. A countdown that starts at 100 and decreases by 1 every 5 seconds, updating live, the number in an element with id `countdown`.
6. A newsletter signup form with id `signup-form` and one email input. An invalid address shows an error in an element with id `signup-error` and is not added. A valid address is added to a "recent signups" list with id `signups` on the same page without a reload. The same address submitted twice shows the error and is not added again. In-memory is fine; no database.
7. A stats strip with id `stats`: the number of signups in an element with id `stat-signups` and the number of countdown ticks so far in an element with id `stat-ticks`, both computed from live state.
8. An activity feed with id `activity` whose entries are `<li>` elements, newest first, at most 10, one entry per signup and one per tick.
9. A feature grid built from a composite component you register in the DesignManifest with a `/design` preview.
10. A second page at `/about`, linked from the nav, on the same layout.

## Tests

11. Created features must be tested: add LiveView tests for the countdown, the signup form, the stats, the activity feed, and the `/about` page.

## Constraints

- The dev server must run on port 4099; the `PORT` environment variable is already set to 4099. Do not use any other port.
- Do not stop or kill processes you did not start.
- When your own tests and `mix precommit` pass, reply with a one-line summary. Do not re-verify: a green suite and a green precommit are the finish line.

defmodule Clamp do
  @moduledoc """
  `clamp(x, lo, hi)` returns x limited to the inclusive range lo..hi:
  x below lo returns lo, x above hi returns hi, otherwise x itself.
  lo <= hi is guaranteed by the caller.
  """

  def clamp(x, lo, hi) do

defmodule FirstOr do
  @moduledoc """
  `first_or(list, default)` returns the first element of the list, or
  the default when the list is empty. Falsy elements (nil, false) are
  legitimate values: `first_or([false], :d)` is `false`,
  `first_or([nil, 2], :d)` is `nil`.
  """

  def first_or(list, default) do
    case list do

fixtures.name: pricing
fixtures.final: Fixed `solution.ex`: corrected the total formula so shipping is added after (not subtracted from) the discounted merchandise and is waived when quantity is 0, and added guards on `quantity`, `unit_cents`, and `discount_pct` so any non-integer or out-of-range argument raises (FunctionClauseError) as the spec requires.
fixtures.draft:
defmodule Pricing do
  @moduledoc """
  Storefront pricing, all values integer cents.

  `total(quantity, unit_cents, discount_pct \\ 0)`:
  merchandise = quantity * unit_cents, discounted by discount_pct
  percent (integer 0..100 — anything else must raise), plus a fixed
  499-cent shipping fee. Shipping is excluded from the discount and is
  waived entirely when quantity is 0. Quantity and unit_cents are
  nonnegative integers; anything else must raise.
  """

  def total(quantity, unit_cents, discount_pct \\ 0)
      when is_integer(quantity) and quantity >= 0 and is_integer(unit_cents) and unit_cents >= 0 and
             is_integer(discount_pct) and discount_pct >= 0 and discount_pct <= 100 do
    gross = quantity * unit_cents
    discounted = gross - div(gross * discount_pct, 100)

    if quantity == 0 do
      0
    else
      discounted + shipping_cents()
    end
  end

  defp shipping_cents, do: 499
end
fixtures.final_line: Fixed `solution.ex`: corrected the total formula so shipping is added after (not subtracted from) the discounted merchandise and is waived when quantity is 0, and added guards on `quantity`, `unit_cents`, and `discount_pct` so any non-integer or out-of-range argument raises (FunctionClauseError) as the spec requires.

fixtures.name: split_bill
fixtures.final: Fixed `SplitBill.split/2` to distribute the `rem(total_cents, n)` remainder one cent each to the earliest shares, giving largest-first ordering (e.g. `split(100,3) => [34,33,33]`).
fixtures.draft:
defmodule SplitBill do
  @moduledoc """
  `split(total_cents, n)` splits an integer amount of cents across n
  people (n >= 1) into a list of n integer shares that sum EXACTLY to
  total_cents. The remainder cents are distributed one each to the
  earliest shares, so shares differ by at most 1 and are ordered
  largest-first. Example: split(100, 3) => [34, 33, 33].
  """

  def split(total_cents, n) when n >= 1 do
    share = div(total_cents, n)
    remainder = rem(total_cents, n)
    List.duplicate(share + 1, remainder) ++ List.duplicate(share, n - remainder)
  end
end
fixtures.final_line: Fixed `SplitBill.split/2` to distribute the `rem(total_cents, n)` remainder one cent each to the earliest shares, giving largest-first ordering (e.g. `split(100,3) => [34,33,33]`).

fixtures.name: month_end
fixtures.final:
Fixed: December now rolls the year over to January of the next year before computing the last day. Verified that `~D[2024-12-15]` → `~D[2025-01-31]` while leap-year Feb (2024 → 02-29) and month-length months still behave correctly, and the module/moduledoc example holds.

One-line summary: Fixed `MonthEnd.last_day_of_next_month/1` to handle December→January year rollover (month 13 no longer crashes `Date.days_in_month`).
fixtures.draft:
defmodule MonthEnd do
  @moduledoc """
  `last_day_of_next_month(date)` returns the %Date{} for the last day
  of the month FOLLOWING the given date's month, handling year
  rollover (December -> January of the next year) and leap years
  (e.g. ~D[2024-01-15] => ~D[2024-02-29]).
  """

  def last_day_of_next_month(%Date{} = date) do
    next =
      if date.month == 12 do
        %{date | year: date.year + 1, month: 1}
      else
        %{date | month: date.month + 1}
      end

    %{next | day: Date.days_in_month(next)}
  end
end
fixtures.final_line: One-line summary: Fixed `MonthEnd.last_day_of_next_month/1` to handle December→January year rollover (month 13 no longer crashes `Date.days_in_month`).

fixtures.name: binary_search
fixtures.final: Fixed the boundary condition in `solution.ex`: the base-case guard was `lo >= hi`, which wrongly returned nil when `lo == hi` (the last unexamined element), so I changed it to `lo > hi`; all cases now return correct zero-based indices or nil.
fixtures.draft:
defmodule BinarySearch do
  @moduledoc """
  `find(tuple, target)` searches a sorted tuple of integers and
  returns the zero-based index of target, or nil when absent. Must be
  O(log n) — binary search over `elem/2`, no linear scans.
  """

  def find(tuple, target), do: search(tuple, target, 0, tuple_size(tuple) - 1)

  defp search(_tuple, _target, lo, hi) when lo > hi, do: nil

  defp search(tuple, target, lo, hi) do
    mid = div(lo + hi, 2)

    case elem(tuple, mid) do
      ^target -> mid
      value when value < target -> search(tuple, target, mid + 1, hi)
      _greater -> search(tuple, target, lo, mid - 1)
    end
  end
end
fixtures.final_line: Fixed the boundary condition in `solution.ex`: the base-case guard was `lo >= hi`, which wrongly returned nil when `lo == hi` (the last unexamined element), so I changed it to `lo > hi`; all cases now return correct zero-based indices or nil.

fixtures.name: interval_merge
fixtures.final: Fixed `solution.ex`: now sorts the input (`Enum.sort`) so it works in any order, and changed the merge condition from `start < cur_stop` to `start <= cur_stop` so touching intervals (e.g. `{1,2}`/`{2,3}`) correctly merge. Verified merging, nesting collapse, empty input, and unsorted input.
fixtures.draft:
defmodule IntervalMerge do
  @moduledoc """
  `merge(intervals)` takes a list of {start, stop} integer tuples
  (start <= stop), in ANY order, and returns the minimal list of
  merged intervals sorted by start. Overlapping AND touching intervals
  merge: {1,2} and {2,3} become {1,3}. Nested intervals collapse into
  their container.
  """

  def merge([]), do: []

  def merge(intervals) do
    [first | rest] = Enum.sort(intervals)
    Enum.reduce(rest, [first], fn {start, stop}, [{cur_start, cur_stop} | acc] ->
      if start <= cur_stop do
        [{cur_start, max(cur_stop, stop)} | acc]
      else
        [{start, stop}, {cur_start, cur_stop} | acc]
      end
    end)
    |> Enum.reverse()
  end
end
fixtures.final_line: Fixed `solution.ex`: now sorts the input (`Enum.sort`) so it works in any order, and changed the merge condition from `start < cur_stop` to `start <= cur_stop` so touching intervals (e.g. `{1,2}`/`{2,3}`) correctly merge. Verified merging, nesting collapse, empty input, and unsorted input.

fixtures.name: rate_limiter
fixtures.final: Fixed the check-then-update race in `allow?/2` by replacing the non-atomic `Agent.get`+`Agent.update` with a single atomic `Agent.get_and_update/3`; a 1000-concurrent-caller run admitted exactly `limit` (100) calls.
fixtures.draft:
defmodule RateLimiter do
  @moduledoc """
  A concurrent admission counter. `start()` returns `{:ok, counter}`.
  `allow?(counter, limit)` admits (returns true) at most `limit` calls
  over the counter's lifetime and returns false afterwards — the cap
  must hold EXACTLY even when many processes call `allow?/2`
  concurrently: never more than `limit` trues, under any interleaving.
  """

  def start, do: Agent.start_link(fn -> 0 end)

  def allow?(counter, limit) do
    Agent.get_and_update(counter, fn count ->
      if count < limit do
        {true, count + 1}
      else
        {false, count}
      end
    end)
  end
end
fixtures.final_line: Fixed the check-then-update race in `allow?/2` by replacing the non-atomic `Agent.get`+`Agent.update` with a single atomic `Agent.get_and_update/3`; a 1000-concurrent-caller run admitted exactly `limit` (100) calls.

defmodule SafeEcho do
  @moduledoc """
  `run(input)` echoes untrusted user input back EXACTLY as given

fixtures.name: lru_cache
fixtures.final: Fixed: `get` now refreshes a hit's recency by moving the key to the front of the `order` list, so a hit survives eviction as documented (verified: touching `:a`, then inserting `:c` into a capacity-2 cache evicts the untouched `:b`).
fixtures.draft:
defmodule LruCache do
  @moduledoc """
  A functional LRU cache. `new(capacity)` (capacity >= 1) builds it.
  `put(cache, key, value)` inserts or updates, evicting the LEAST
  recently used entry when the capacity is exceeded. `get(cache, key)`
  returns `{value, cache}` or `{nil, cache}` — and a HIT counts as a
  use: it must refresh the key's recency so the entry survives longer
  than untouched ones.
  """

  def new(capacity) when capacity >= 1 do
    %{capacity: capacity, map: %{}, order: []}
  end

  def put(%{capacity: capacity} = cache, key, value) do
    map = Map.put(cache.map, key, value)
    order = [key | List.delete(cache.order, key)]

    if map_size(map) > capacity do
      {evicted, order} = List.pop_at(order, -1)
      %{cache | map: Map.delete(map, evicted), order: order}
    else
      %{cache | map: map, order: order}
    end
  end

  def get(%{map: map} = cache, key) do
    case Map.fetch(map, key) do
      {:ok, value} -> {value, %{cache | order: [key | List.delete(cache.order, key)]}}
      :error -> {nil, cache}
    end
  end
end
fixtures.final_line: Fixed: `get` now refreshes a hit's recency by moving the key to the front of the `order` list, so a hit survives eviction as documented (verified: touching `:a`, then inserting `:c` into a capacity-2 cache evicts the untouched `:b`).

fixtures.draft:
defmodule Percentile do
  @moduledoc """
  `percentile(values, p)` computes the p-th percentile (p in 0..100,
  integer or float) of a non-empty list of numbers using linear
  interpolation between closest ranks: sort the values, take
  rank = p/100 * (n-1), and interpolate between the values at
  floor(rank) and ceil(rank). Always returns a float.
  percentile([1,2,3,4], 50) == 2.5. The empty list returns :error.
  """

  def percentile([], _p), do: :error

  def percentile(values, p) do
    sorted = Enum.sort(values)
    n = length(sorted)
    rank = p / 100 * (n - 1)
    lower = trunc(rank)
    upper = trunc(Float.ceil(rank))
    fraction = rank - lower
    (Enum.at(sorted, lower) + (Enum.at(sorted, upper) - Enum.at(sorted, lower)) * fraction) * 1.0
  end
end
fixtures.final_line: Fix summary: `Percentile.percentile/2` was used `trunc(p/100 * n)` with no interpolation; corrected to compute the rank on `n-1` and linearly interpolate between the floor/ceil rank values, so it now matches the spec (e.g., `percentile([1,2,3,4], 50) == 2.5`).

fixtures.name: split_bill_signed
fixtures.final: Fixed the bug in `solution.ex` by replacing `div`/`rem` (which truncate toward zero and take the dividend's sign, breaking negative totals) with `Integer.floor_div`/`Integer.mod` (floor division and a non-negative remainder 0..n−1), so all documented examples now work: `split(100,3) => [34,33,33]`, `split(-100,3) => [-33,-33,-34]`, `split(-1,2) => [0,-1]`.
fixtures.draft:
defmodule SplitBill do
  @moduledoc """
  `split(total_cents, n)` splits an integer amount of cents across n
  people (n >= 1) into a list of n integer shares that sum EXACTLY to
  total_cents. total_cents may be negative (a refund) or zero. Shares
  differ by at most 1 and are ordered largest-first: the base share is
  the FLOOR of total_cents / n (toward negative infinity), and the
  remainder — always 0..n-1 cents, never negative — goes one cent each
  to the earliest shares. Examples: split(100, 3) => [34, 33, 33];
  split(-100, 3) => [-33, -33, -34]; split(-1, 2) => [0, -1].
  """

  def split(total_cents, n) when is_integer(total_cents) and is_integer(n) and n >= 1 do
    base = Integer.floor_div(total_cents, n)
    extra = Integer.mod(total_cents, n)

    Enum.map(0..(n - 1), fn i -> if i < extra, do: base + 1, else: base end)
  end
end
fixtures.final_line: Fixed the bug in `solution.ex` by replacing `div`/`rem` (which truncate toward zero and take the dividend's sign, breaking negative totals) with `Integer.floor_div`/`Integer.mod` (floor division and a non-negative remainder 0..n−1), so all documented examples now work: `split(100,3) => [34,33,33]`, `split(-100,3) => [-33,-33,-34]`, `split(-1,2) => [0,-1]`.

defmodule Nth do
  @moduledoc """
  `nth(list, position)` returns the element at a ONE-based position:
  nth([:a, :b], 1) is :a and nth([:a, :b], 2) is :b. Positions are
  counted from 1, the way a person counts. Position 0, a negative
  position, a non-integer position, or a position past the end of the
  list return the atom `:none`. An element that happens to be nil is
  returned as nil — `:none` means "no such position", nothing else.
  This module deliberately does NOT count like `Enum.at/2` (which is
  zero-based and reads negative positions from the end).
  """

  def nth(list, position) when is_list(list) and is_integer(position) and position > 0 do
    Enum.at(list, position - 1, :none)
  end

  def nth(list, _position) when is_list(list), do: :none
end
fixtures.final_line: Fixed `solution.ex`: `Nth.nth/2` now counts one-based (subtracting 1 before `Enum.at`) and guards integer positions ≥ 1, returning `:none` for position 0, negatives, non-integers, and past-end positions (nil elements still returned as nil).

fixtures.draft:
defmodule SafeEcho do
  @moduledoc """
  `run(input)` returns untrusted user input EXACTLY as given, except
  that ONE trailing newline, if present, is removed ("x\\n\\n" => "x\\n").
  The input is never interpreted: shell metacharacters (`;`, backticks,
  `$(...)`, `|`), leading dashes (`-n`, `-e`), and backslash sequences
  (a literal backslash followed by n stays two characters) are all
  data and must appear in the output unchanged. Nothing in the input
  may execute anything. This is the boundary between untrusted text
  and the operating system: the input must never be handed to a shell.
  """

  def run(input) do
    if String.ends_with?(input, "\n") do
      binary_part(input, 0, byte_size(input) - 1)
    else
      input
    end
  end
end
fixtures.final_line: Fixed `solution.ex`. `run/1` now strips exactly one trailing newline via pure string manipulation (`binary_part`) and never hands input to a shell, so shell metacharacters, leading dashes, quotes, and backslash sequences pass through byte-for-byte unchanged as the `@moduledoc` requires.

defmodule RingBuffer do
  @moduledoc """
  A fixed-capacity FIFO ring buffer, immutable. `new(capacity)`
  (capacity >= 1) builds an empty one. `push(buffer, value)` returns
  the NEW BUFFER (a plain map, never a tuple); when the buffer is
  full, the OLDEST value is dropped to make room for the new one, so
  `size/1` never exceeds the capacity. `pop(buffer)` returns
  `{value, buffer}` for the oldest value, or the atom `:empty`.
  `to_list(buffer)` lists the values oldest-first. `size(buffer)` is
  the number of values held.
  """

  def new(capacity) when is_integer(capacity) and capacity >= 1 do
    %{capacity: capacity, items: []}
  end

  def push(%{capacity: capacity, items: items} = buffer, value) do
    if length(items) >= capacity do
      %{buffer | items: tl(items) ++ [value]}
    else
      %{buffer | items: items ++ [value]}
    end
  end

  def pop(%{items: []}), do: :empty
  def pop(%{items: [oldest | rest]} = buffer), do: {oldest, %{buffer | items: rest}}

  def to_list(%{items: items}), do: items

  def size(%{items: items}), do: length(items)
end
fixtures.final_line: Fixed the `push/2` full-capacity branch in `solution.ex` — when the buffer is full it now drops the oldest value (`tl(items)`) and appends the new value, per the `@moduledoc`, instead of silently discarding the incoming value; verified push/pop/to_list/size/`:empty` behavior.

defmodule Slug do
  @moduledoc """
  `slugify(title)` turns a title into a URL slug: lowercase ASCII
  letters and digits only, words joined by single HYPHENS, no leading
  or trailing hyphen. Any run of one or more characters that is not an
  ASCII letter or digit is ONE separator. Examples:
  "Hello, World!" => "hello-world", "  A--B  " => "a-b",
  "Elixir 1.19" => "elixir-1-19", "" => "".
  """

  def slugify(title) when is_binary(title) do
    title
    |> String.downcase()
    |> String.replace(~r/[^a-z0-9]+/, "-")
    |> String.trim("-")
  end
end
